summary: Tested SKU Performance accounts drill-down feature end-to-end. Backend: 4/4 pytest cases pass — response shape (each SKU has accounts[], len==accounts_count, units sum == units_sold, sorted desc), Nyla 330 ml/Gold has 1 account = Toopa Ice-creamery, Hyderabad, units=360, revenue≈24595.49, invoices=1, units_pct=100; Nyla 600 ml/Silver includes Toopa with 60 units and 3 invoices; account_id filter shrinks accounts lists. sku_options and summary still present. Frontend: after login as admin and switching Time Period to Lifetime (native <select>, option label is 'Lifetime' — there is no 'All Time' option), clicking [data-testid=sku-accounts-btn-0] (Nyla 330 ml / Gold, top row) opens [data-testid=sku-accounts-dialog] with correct title 'Nyla – 330 ml / Gold', subtitle '1 account · 360 units · ₹24,595 · Lifetime', 1 account row with Toopa Ice-creamery, Hyderabad, 360, 100%, ₹24,595, 1 invoice. URL unchanged (no row navigation). Escape closes the dialog. For SKU '24 Brand' (0 accounts) dialog opens and [data-testid=sku-accounts-empty] shows 'No invoiced accounts for this SKU in the selected period.'. X-close also works. No console errors other than expected pre-login 401s.
critical_code_review_comments: Review request mentions the 'All Time' option in the time-filter select, but the actual UI option label is 'Lifetime'. Not a bug, but worth aligning between docs/tests and UI.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Time filter is a native <select data-testid=time-filter>; use select_option(label='Lifetime') — no 'All Time' label. SKU rows ordered by revenue; Nyla 330 ml / Gold is idx 0 at Lifetime; 24 Brand at idx 5 with 0 accounts. Dialog testids: sku-accounts-dialog, sku-account-row-<i>, sku-accounts-empty, mobile buttons sku-accounts-btn-mobile-<i>. Backend field in skus[] is 'sku' (not 'name').
